analysis: The PR is docs-only: docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (patch at lines 228-283) and docs/reference/configuration.md (excerpt at lines 503-576). It documents a large-memory default for complete-checkpoint staging caps: 7168 MiB and 15000 ms on Macs with at least 96 GiB, replacing 1024 MiB and 1000 ms. An explicit DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB or _MS overrides both cap families. The caps gate capture and read, so file sizes and transient staging RAM grow, and there is no permanent carve. The overrides are not forwarded to LaunchAgents. The documented design leaves AES-GCM/DBK3 format, HMAC tags, the 30-minute TTL, the daily write cap, the account-scoped salt and identity binding unchanged, so T-041 leak #1 and leak #2 are unaffected. The only threat-model gap is that the larger transient RAM, disk and staging time are not recorded in the T-041 mitigations. The code changes (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift, SSDHybridCheckpointStoreFactory.swift, SSDHybridCheckpointStore.acceptsCheckpoint) were not supplied. The next pass should verify that the reservation and refusal paths still fall back to recompute, that the explicit-override precedence is correct, and that the 20 GiB disk floor and write budget still apply to the larger files.

findings.detail: The docs now say complete checkpoints on Macs with at least 96 GiB default to a 7168 MiB payload cap and a 15000 ms estimated-read cap, up from 1024 MiB and 1000 ms. The cap gates both capture and read. Cache files are written from consumer-driven donations. T-041 and its 'no persistent memory carve / bounded staging' mitigation describe transient RAM only as bounded and give no size. A single read can now reserve about 7 GiB of native destination plus scratch in GlobalKVCacheBudget. A single donation or write can reach about 7 GiB of host buffers and disk. Either could degrade concurrent serving or fill the disk (T-016) until the 20 GiB floor stops writes. The 4000 GB/day write cap and the half-free-space disk budget are unchanged. The threat model should record the new bounds and confirm that reservation refusal still falls back to recompute. The source change itself was not supplied, so this cannot be confirmed from this PR.
findings.title: Raised complete-checkpoint staging caps (7 GiB / 15 s on Macs with at least 96 GiB) are not reflected in the T-041 bounded-staging posture
